about: The story-event engine's content (#34; engine: webapp/js/core/story/story-engine.js). EVERYTHING HERE IS A STAND-IN: a sample of Act 1's opening that proves every piece; not the real story. A new event, thread, card or person is one more entry; story-engine.js validate() is the rulebook and the tests run it. The story REMEMBERS through story state (flags, quests, seen, choices) and the map (data/places.json) opens places from those flags; a place's go: { story: <spot> } walks into one of the spots below. Things are given only by story grants (data/progress.json 'story', items in data/items.json). 18+ entries and 'agreed beforehand' entries never ship here: they are the owner's.

stroll.name: Take a walk
nothing: Nothing much. The street minds its own business.
A quiet walk. Somewhere, a vending machine argues with a customer.
You walk. The city hums. Nobody needs anything from you for once.

talk.name: Talk to {who}
nothing: Busy. A grunt, a nod, back to work.

home.name: Spend the evening in
nothing: A quiet evening. The roof only leaks in one place tonight.

voyage.name: Sail a while
nothing: Flat water, a fair wind. Nothing but gulls.
The bay keeps its secrets today.

al.name: Old Man Al
al.line: A tinkerer who knows too much and looks at her too little.

inspector.name: the inspector
inspector.line: Citizen Pass compliance. A hard job he doesn't always agree with.

fisher.name: the old fisherman
fisher.line: Has out-waited every fish in the bay and most of the people.

courier.name: the courier
courier.line: Watches from doorways. Carries things nobody signs for.

scrapper.name: a scrapper
scrapper.line: Thinks your salvage is his salvage.

jester.line: A face on every screen at once.

tells.found_her: He found the other her, in that world.
tells.met_someone: He met someone new in the story.
tells.new_place: He reached somewhere new in the story.
tells.gift: He gave the other her a small gift.
tells.close_call: Something in the story went badly for a moment.
tells.she_saved_him: The other her saved him in a fight.
tells.took_care: He lost a fight and the other her took care of him.
tells.game_over: A fight in the story beat him and he had to try again.
tells.promise_made: A promise was made in the story.
tells.promise_kept: A promise was kept in the story.
tells.echo: He played through a glimpse of another timeline.
tells.old_friend: Someone from earlier in the story came back.
tells.broadcast: Someone took over every screen in the story.
tells.chapter_end: A chapter of the story ended.

the_hum.name: Her nervous hum
the_hum.line: Al knew she hums when she's nervous before you'd ever heard it.

shrines.name: Al's junk sculptures
shrines.line: She went quiet in front of one of them and couldn't say why.

not_this_time.name: "Not this time."
not_this_time.line: What Al mutters before every danger. Counted, never explained (yet).

excuses.name: She never quite hits them
excuses.line: Every time a person gets hurt around her, she has a reason it wasn't her. Counted for the reveal.

name_slip.name: The wrong name
name_slip.line: Al called her something she's never been called, then covered it up.

wave_sign.name: The wave on the walls
wave_sign.line: An old wave symbol painted around the slums. Nobody can say what it means.

stranger.name: The woman in the doorway
stranger.line: She's been watching you. She hasn't decided about you yet.

inspector.name: The inspector looked away
inspector.line: He let an unregistered android walk. He remembers how you asked.

fisher_crew.name: "Not now."
fisher_crew.line: The old fisherman won't crew for someone who hasn't sailed. Yet.

promise_steer.name: A promise: she steers next time
promise_steer.line: She said next time out, she's steering. She meant it.

ch1_start.title: Chapter 1: Things people throw away
text: Status: found. Location: a bin. Finder: {you}. I've had better launches.
Chapter one. He dug me out of a pile of scrap. I'm choosing to call that an entrance.

act1_end.title: End of the sample: the boat is ready
text: We have a boat, a harbor, an old man who won't look at me, and a clown on every screen. ...Previously on: everything was simpler.

p_jun.title: {her}
text: That's me. Unregistered. Slightly dented. Fully operational where it counts.
Me. I'd write more but I'm biased.

p_al.title: Old Man Al
text: Fixes everything. Looks at everything. Except me. I'm keeping count.
Grumpy. Brilliant. Knows what's wrong with my cooling before I do. Suspicious.

p_inspector.title: The inspector
text: He checked his scanner twice and saw nothing, twice. Bad at his job. I like him.

p_fisher.title: The old fisherman
text: Says "not now" like other people say hello. Smells like the tide. Gave us a lure.

p_courier.title: The courier
text: She watched us for days before saying a word. I respect the patience. I don't like being the one watched.
A face on every screen. She looked straight at me and winked. I didn't like how familiar it felt.

pl_scrapyard.title: The scrapyard
text: Where the city puts what it's done with. Present company included.
Everything here was somebody's future once. Good salvage, though.

pl_workshop.title: Old Man Al's workshop
text: Junk sculptures on every shelf. One of them made my chest go quiet. I didn't mention it.

pl_port_buffer.title: Port Buffer
text: A dead harbor with one good plank. We fixed a second one. It's a start.
First impression: rust. Second impression: possibility. Third: more rust.

pl_bay.title: Brandwater Bay
text: Water. A lot of it. I'm 40% electricity. We're going anyway.

c_crawler.title: Cable crawler
text: Follows you. Chews wiring. I took it personally.

n_memo.title: A memo in the rubble
text: "Harbor 3 closure: not profitable enough. Please vacate by Friday. Thank you for being part of the Everything family."

n_ledger_1.title: A torn ledger page
text: Tally marks, hundreds of them. Under the last row, in a shaking hand: "the lamp. She laughed at the lamp. Remember that one."

care.name: You lost a fight: she takes care of you
care.line: On Easy nothing is lost. She gets you home and patches you up.

beats.t: I told him to back off. He didn't listen. Nobody listens.
Hold still. This is the part that stings.
There. You're staying in tonight. That wasn't a question.
You didn't come back, so I came to get you. Don't make it a thing.
...There you are. No. Head stays where it is.
My lap is not a pillow. This is a medical position.
...You can stay a little longer. For medical reasons.

coming_home.name: Coming home
coming_home.line: The quiet end of a day out. One of the safe-spot moments.

beats.t: Sit. I made the hot leaf water. It's supposed to be relaxing.
...Is it? I can't tell. Tell me if it's relaxing.
Boots off. You're tracking the whole scrapyard in.
...It was a good day, though. Don't tell anyone I said so.
I'm not leaning on you. The wall is cold. You're the closest warm thing.

wake.text: Morning in the slums. The roof leaks in the usual place. Your Citizen Pass pings before you've opened both eyes.

ping.text: "Good morning, valued citizen! Your score has been updated. Reason: insufficient enthusiasm. Have an Everything day!"

choices.text: Same as yesterday. Get up anyway.
"Thank you for your enthusiasm about my enthusiasm."
Mute it. It un-mutes itself. Of course it does.

out.text: With a score like yours, there's one place that still lets you work: the scrapyard, where the city leaves what it's done with.

ship.text: A corporate hauler drops out of the smog, far too clean for this sky. It dumps one load over the east heap and is gone before the dust lands.

pile.text: Fresh scrap. Unmarked crates, cut cables, and under all of it, a hand.

choices.text: Check the casing first. This is worth more than a year of scrap.

text: ...Diagnostic. Location: a bin. Outlook: poor. Who are you?
...Systems up. I'm in a pile of trash. You're staring. One of us should say something.

text.t: {you}. Fine. You were careful with my arm. I noticed. Don't make it weird.

text: {you}. Fine. I don't have a name on file for me. That's probably bad.

al_hint.text: She can't walk straight: something in her leg whines with every step. There's one person in the slums who fixes things nobody else will touch.

door.text: Shelves of junk sculptures, each one bolted together with more care than junk deserves. An old man doesn't look up from his bench.

al1.text: "Put her on the bench. Left leg. Stabilizer coil, I'd bet my good eye." He hasn't looked at her once.

quiet.text: She has stopped in front of one of the sculptures. A ribbon is tied around it. She doesn't say anything. She's humming, very quietly.

slip.text: "She always hums when she's nervous." A beat too late, he adds: "...They all do. That model."

choices.text: "How would you know what she always does?"

dodge.text: "I know machines." He turns a screw that didn't need turning.

projects.text: "Projects." He moves between you and the shelf. "Don't touch them."

job.text: "I can't fix that leg with what I've got. There's a coil that fits in the scrapyard's buried levels. Bring it and I'll have her running by supper." Under his breath, to nobody: "Not this time."

evening.text: She's sitting on the one good crate, leg stretched out, cataloguing your shack out loud. "One window. One pot. One person. Minimalist."

give.text: You've been turning something over in your pocket all day.

choices.text: A ribbon you found, still clean.
A hair clip, one tooth missing.
A bolt you bent into a ring. Sort of.

text: A {gift}. For me. ...Why. No, don't explain. I'm keeping it. Obviously I'm keeping it.
"A {gift}." She holds it like it might be a trick. It isn't. She keeps holding it.

text.t: "Hold still." She waits for the light from the window, then something clicks behind her eyes. "There. That one's a keeper."

text: "Hold still." Something clicks behind her eyes. "There. Now we're even. I have one of you. Mostly. My thumb was in it."

hatch.text: Behind the east heap, a hatch somebody welded shut and somebody else cut open again. Stairs go down.

text.t: "I'll scan. You walk in front. That's teamwork."

text: You go down alone. She'd wanted to come; her leg had other ideas.

got.text: At the bottom, still in its cradle: the coil. And something that chews cable, which you've now met.

partial.text: You come back up early with a coil from a wrecked unit near the stairs. Scorched, but the right kind. It'll do.

carried.text: You wake up at home. There's a coil on the table and scrapes on her knuckles. "You dropped it. I picked it up. We're not discussing how."

fit.text: He fits the coil without looking anything up. "Don't run her hard in the rain for a week. That housing leaks when it's new." He says it like he's watched it happen.

walk.text: She crosses the workshop without the whine. Then back, faster. Then a turn that is definitely showing off. "Acceptable," she says, to Al's back.

harbor.text: "You two want off scrap wages? There's a dead harbor past the pump road. Port Buffer. Half a dock, one good hull if nobody's burned it. The sea still pays people the Pass doesn't."

stop.text: "Citizen. Routine compliance." A grey coat, a scanner, tired eyes. The scanner swings toward her and chirps: NO PASS ON FILE.

choices.text: "She was thrown away. I found her. That's all of it."
Hold out the few credits you have.

honest.text: He looks at her for a long moment. "Scanner's been faulty all week." He taps it against his palm until it stops chirping.

toaster.text: "Ding," she says, flatly. The inspector's mouth does something he clearly didn't authorize. "...Faulty scanner. All week."

bribe.text: "Put that away. You need it more than I do, and I'd have to report us both." He turns the scanner off himself.

after.text: "Get her papers, or keep her out of the main roads on audit days. I didn't say which days. I don't know which days." He walks on.

arrive.text: Port Buffer. Gull-white pilings, a crane rusted mid-reach, and one stretch of dock that still holds weight.

memo.text: Under a fallen sign, a laminated notice has outlived everything it was nailed to.

build.text: The planks are stacked where someone left them, years ago, meaning to come back.

fisher.text: By the time the last plank is down, an old man is sitting on the end of your dock as if it had always been there. "Hm. Holds." He hands you a lure without looking away from the water.

choices.text: "We'll need hands when we sail. Interested?"

notnow.text: "Not now." He reels in nothing, contentedly. "Ask me when you've been out there and come back."

hull.text: "There's a hull under that tarp. Dinghy. It has a hole in it, but only the one."

patch.text: Pitch, a patch, and a mallet. The trick is the timing.

tight.text: "Watertight. First try. Who taught you that? Don't say me, I'll get smug."

fine.text: "It weeps a little. So do most boats. It floats."

again.text: "That's your thumb. That's the patch. Different things." She holds the patch for the second try, and it takes.

promise.text: She runs a hand along the gunwale. "First time out, you row. I'm 40% electricity. But next time? I'm steering."

out.text: "Heading: out. Weather: mostly fine. Me: fine. Stop looking at me, look at the water."

loop.text: Once around the near buoys and back. From out here the slums are a smudge and the harbor is yours.

short.text: The chop turns you around at the first buoy. "That counts," she says, gripping the seat. "We went. We came back. That's a voyage."

flicker.text: Every screen in sight flickers at once: the billboards, the Pass kiosk, a dead monitor in a heap that hasn't worked in years.

face.text: "Gooood evening, valued audience! We interrupt your regularly scheduled despair. A little boat went out today. A little boat came back. I just love a show with legs." The face looks straight at her. "Hi, Sis."

gone.text: The screens go back to their ads. She hasn't moved. She's humming.

text: A wave, painted in one stroke on a shutter. Old paint, under newer ads. Someone keeps scraping the ads off it.
The same wave again, low on a wall where a child or a kneeling adult would paint it.
A wave scratched into a lamp post. You'd have walked past it a week ago.
"That symbol isn't in any registry I can reach. Somebody wanted it forgotten properly."
"Again. Whoever paints these isn't selling anything. That's the strange part."

woman.text: An old woman repainting a shutter catches you looking at the wave beside it.

told.text: "It means people stood together once and got erased for it. We don't talk about the docks." She goes back to painting. She leaves the wave alone.

nod.text: She nods back, and you both let it be. The wave will still be there tomorrow.

text: A billboard: "EVERYTHING WATER. Now with 30% more water!"
A kiosk chirps: "Terms Update 41 is here! By continuing to exist, you agree."
A poster: "Lonely? Everything Inc cares. Loneliness Plus, first month free."
A drone trails a banner: "Your score could be worse! Don't find out how."
"I'd file a complaint, but the complaint form is also an ad."
"I ran the numbers. The numbers are also sponsored."
"Don't read it. Reading it counts as agreeing."

watch.text: A woman in a courier's jacket leans in a doorway across the street. She isn't looking at you. She's looking at who you're with.

gone.text: By the time the next cart passes, the doorway is empty.

stranger_again.name: The woman in the doorway, again

text.t: The courier again, in a different doorway. "Still not now? I can wait. I'm good at it."
The courier steps out of the doorway this time. "You nodded. Most people pretend I'm a wall."

text: The courier steps out of the doorway this time. "You two are easy to follow. That's a problem you should fix."

ask.text: "I move things for people the Pass doesn't see. Some day you'll need something moved, or I will. That's all. Now we've met."

text.t: The inspector falls into step beside you, eyes forward. "You were straight with me. So: main road, tomorrow, a sweep. Take the pump road."
The inspector passes you without stopping. A folded note lands in your hand: "Sweep tomorrow. Main road. Keep your credits."

text: The inspector stops to retie a boot that didn't need it. "If I owned an advanced toaster, I'd keep it off the main road tomorrow."

now.text: "Saw you go out. Saw you come back." He stands, which seems to take most of a minute. "Now."

tiller.text: She's already at the tiller when you step aboard. "You promised. Well. I promised. Same thing. Sit."

sail.text: She steers like she's defusing something, then like she's done it all her life, in the space of a hundred meters.

text: A crate rides low in the swell, stamped EVERYTHING INC: RETURNS.
Something square bobs off the port side, trailing kelp like a wig.
Inside: forty identical left gloves.
Inside: a waterlogged manual for a product that was never released.
Inside: sealed ration bars, best before a year that hasn't happened yet.

lost.text: It rolls under and is gone. The bay keeps that one.

fog.text: The fog comes in sideways and takes the shore with it.

choices.text: "You navigate. I'll row where you point."
Ship the oars and wait it out.
Turn for where the harbor was.

nav.text: "Two points left. More. Stop. ...That was a rock. You're welcome." She sounds terrified and delighted in equal parts.

wait.text: It thins in its own time. It always does. The harbor is right where you left it.

text: "I counted the leaks. Four. I named them. Don't ask."
"I reorganized your pot. There's only one pot. It took a while."
She doesn't say anything, which from her is a kind of compliment.
After a while she starts humming. Not the nervous one. A different one.

kiss.text: "...Unauthorized." She doesn't move away. "Log it under maintenance."

text: Nothing needs doing tonight. That's rare enough that you both notice.
The roof isn't leaking. The street is quiet. The evening is, suspiciously, free.

morning.text: Morning comes in sideways through the gap in the shutters. Neither of you made it to bed, and neither of you minds.

text: "That counted as doing something. I'm logging it as doing something."
"Same time tomorrow. Or whenever. I'm flexible. I'm not, but say I am."

pot.text: She has found a recipe. She is holding it like a summons.

text: The pot is empty. The one pot. It did its best.
Dishes: one pot, two spoons. She washes; you dry; nobody drops anything.
"That cooling unit you're eyeing? Fails in the rain. Trust me." He doesn't say how he knows.
"Solder from the cold side. She'll thank you. Not out loud."
"Crying over a damn bot," he mutters at something on his bench, and then notices you're there.

slip.text: "Tell Jo I said—" He stops. "Tell her. Tell {her} to watch that knee." He goes back to work very hard.

block.text: A scrapper steps out from behind a heap with a length of pipe. "East heap's mine. Whatever's in that bag is mine. Simple."

choices.text: "There's enough scrap here for two lifetimes. Walk away."
Hand him a bent bolt. "Finest piece in the bag."
Put the bag down and don't move.

talked.text: He weighs it, and you, and the android standing very still beside you. "...Tomorrow, then." He doesn't come back tomorrow.

t: He goes down over her foot, which wasn't there a second ago. "I tripped," she says. "Into him. It happens."
His pipe ends up in her hand and he ends up sitting. "He dropped it. I caught it. Reflexes."

text: He overreaches, and you're still standing when he isn't. He leaves the pipe.

savedby.text: The pipe is coming down and then it isn't: she's holding the other end. She doesn't hit him. She just doesn't let go until he does. "...You're bleeding. Home. Now."

home.text: The scrapyard keeps the bag. No: she went back for the bag. Of course she did.

glitch.text: The room stutters. For a moment the light is colder, the walls are different, and your hands are not your hands.

lamp.text: A workbench. A lamp in pieces. A younger man's hands, and beside them an android with shorter hair and a ribbon you don't recognize, holding the shade like evidence.

laugh.text: She laughs: at the lamp, at you, at the rain starting on a roof that isn't yours. It is the easiest sound in the world. Static creeps in at the edges. Then the room is your room again.

after.text: "...I think I just watched someone else's memory. Rude." She's quiet for a while after that.
